What changed in the current framework?

This site currently reflects PapersMinimal v3.077, with ProofChainAudits v1.83, DAG Atlas v1.223, and S³ Structure Network v1.49. The manuscript update is dated 20 November 2026. The current archive contains 31 active papers across seven volumes.

The important point is not simply that files have newer version numbers. In the latest source, several finite constructions became more explicit. They may strengthen the geometric route to observables, but their independently audited scope and their physical occurrence still have to be distinguished.

Five-core geometry and transition direction

In Paper I–B, the revised source develops the resistance and comparison structure of a five-core network, its reversible Laplacian, and the relationship to oriented input/output ports. The source-cyclic Schur return is an exact finite comparison construction. A reversible comparison kernel is not by itself a physical decay arrow. The observed direction and strength of a decay require the appropriate dynamics and source.

Localization and finite measurement outcomes

Paper II–C now includes a reduction of compact finite-dimensional continuous-outcome POVMs to finite positive representatives preserving the relevant effect-span rank, together with intrinsic-position rank thresholds and a fixed-radius approximation limit. This extends a mathematical localization constraint; it does not establish that a particular detector or measurement process occurs physically.

Dynamics and reference subtraction

Paper III–F examines the fixed-background off-diagonal nonmetric matter current in an adopted reference-subtracted action family. Under the stated source conditions, the nonmetric matter vertices and transition matrix elements are insensitive to that subtraction. This is a useful consistency result within the chosen action family; it does not settle metric variations or the selection of the physical action.

Hadrons and the missing physical current

The most extensive recent additions are in Paper VII–A and Paper VII–B. They cover source-cyclic compression, Schur vertices, Ward conditions, Hurwitz baryon structures, root-normalized diagnostics, a 56-state decuplet–octet tensor, and conditional axial transition strengths and bounds.

The distinction is crucial: the current source provides geometric and operator comparison strengths, not a table of unconditional decay widths or lifetimes. It explicitly retains the need for the physically selected Gauss-reduced source/current, the complete mixed-current moments, actual poles, open-channel absorptive continuation, and a common absolute normalization. Neither mass differences alone nor scalar overlap are promoted into a decay amplitude.

What the updated verification data means

The current DAG release carries 14,366 distinct source labels and a 7,667-node inherited canonical graph. It adds current-source anchors for 55 newly integrated labels without adding new certified canonical proof edges or promoting physical occurrence claims. The separate audit archive contains versioned reports and 130 recorded remaining-obligation rows; these are not a new E3/E4 audit of all v3.077 text.

Use the research explorer to find the 55 new statements, the paper library to inspect the source, and the verification browser to find historical proof obligations. For exact scope, the versioned manuscripts and audit records remain authoritative.

Particle and hadron research, connected visually

The separately editable matter geometry guide connects the complete 2O working elementary-particle response to the current 2I/600-cell hadron-source comparisons through their common 2T Hurwitz core, without incorrectly embedding 2O inside 2I. It illustrates the heavy, middle and light split grammars using the supplied X-posts visual archive. It also explains the Paper VII-A/VII-B finite three-face baryon membrane, heat-reference overlap, Gram-normalized current cancellation and source-visible pole tests. These finite operators are not yet a prediction of observed partial widths, and the latest source integration remains unaudited at E3/E4 as a block.
